target.title: feat: add WhatsApp phone-code login
target.body:
Closes #85867

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users trying to connect WhatsApp from a headless, remote, or QR-unavailable environment had no first-class login path. OpenClaw only exposed the WhatsApp QR flow, so users who could not scan a QR code could not link WhatsApp even though WhatsApp Linked Devices supports phone-number pairing.

It also fixes a session-state edge case where partial phone-code pairing credentials could look linked enough to block a clean retry, even though the WhatsApp account was not fully registered.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a typed channel login method for phone-number login, exposes it through `openclaw channels login whatsapp --phone-number <number>`, and keeps QR login as the default path. The generic CLI/channel contract carries a structured `phone-number` login method, while the WhatsApp plugin owns the Baileys `requestPairingCode` implementation, pairing-code display, retry behavior, and cleanup of stale partial pairing credentials.

The change intentionally keeps WhatsApp-specific policy inside the WhatsApp plugin and only adds the small shared channel-auth contract needed for channels to advertise and receive non-QR login methods.

## User Impact

Users can now link WhatsApp by entering their phone number in the CLI and then entering the generated code in WhatsApp's Linked Devices flow. QR login still works for users who prefer it or have a scannable terminal session.

If a phone-code attempt leaves behind incomplete credentials, the next login can clear that stale partial state and let the user retry instead of treating the account as already connected.

## Evidence

- Focused Testbox proof passed on Blacksmith Testbox lease `tbx_01kwx37srehytb7qgb8nt9y9j0`:
  - `pnpm test src/cli/channel-auth.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auth-store.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/login.test.ts src/channels/plugins/contracts/channel-catalog.contract.test.ts`
- Changed-surface gate passed on the same Testbox lease:
  - `pnpm check:changed`
- Whitespace check passed:
  - `git diff --check`
- Local autoreview completed clean after fixing the accepted findings it raised:
  - phone-code replacement sockets now issue a fresh code after a timeout
  - readiness handling no longer misses an immediate pairing-ready event during socket creation
  - QR-linked credentials with a usable identity still count as linked

Remaining proof gap: I did not run a live WhatsApp physical-device pairing smoke on this replacement branch. The implementation is covered by focused tests and changed-surface checks, but live pairing should still be verified before merge.
